questions.question: Compare the pandemic potential of SARS-CoV-2 with that of MERS-CoV.

parts.text: Give three reasons that SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into a worldwide pandemic and MERS-CoV did not.

parts_raw.text: Give three reasons that SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into a worldwide pandemic and MERS-CoV did not.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Efficient sustained human-to-human transmission: SARS-CoV-2 uses ACE2, abundantly expressed on upper respiratory epithelium, giving high-titre nasopharyngeal shedding and effective respiratory droplet/aerosol spread (R0 ~2-3+), whereas MERS-CoV uses DPP4, expressed mainly in the lower respiratory tract, so human-to-human transmission is inefficient (R0 <1) and largely confined to healthcare and household contact. (2) Pre-symptomatic and asymptomatic/mildly symptomatic transmission: peak SARS-CoV-2 viral load occurs at or just before symptom onset, so a large proportion of transmission occurs before illness is recognized and cannot be interrupted by symptom-based case detection and isolation; MERS cases are typically severely ill and transmit late in illness, when they are already identified and isolated. (3) Reservoir/exposure and case-severity epidemiology: MERS requires repeated zoonotic introduction from dromedary camels, geographically restricted to the Arabian Peninsula and associated with a high case fatality (~35%) that limits onward spread, whereas SARS-CoV-2 established a global human chain of transmission out of a densely populated, highly connected hub with intense international air travel, and its comparatively low case fatality with a wide spectrum of mild illness allowed infected people to remain mobile and seed new populations.

questions.question: MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 are both coronaviruses.

parts.text: What are three reasons, not social or related to pandemic management, why SARS-CoV-2 is so different, i.e. why it caused a pandemic?

parts_raw.text: MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 are both coronaviruses. What are 3 reasons that aren’t social or pandemic management for why SARS-CoV-2 is so different, i.e why it caused a pandemic?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Receptor: SARS-CoV-2 spike uses ACE2, highly expressed in the upper airway, giving high nasopharyngeal viral loads and easy droplet/aerosol spread; MERS-CoV uses DPP4, concentrated in the lower respiratory tract. (2) Intrinsic transmissibility: efficient sustained human-to-human spread (R0 approximately 2-3), aided by the polybasic furin cleavage site at the S1/S2 junction; MERS-CoV requires repeated camel-to-human introductions and has R0 <1. (3) Pre-symptomatic/asymptomatic shedding with peak viral load around symptom onset and a comparatively low case-fatality rate, so infected people transmit while well; MERS causes severe, readily recognized illness (CFR about 35%) with transmission late in disease.

questions.question: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV a worse global threat than MERS-CoV?
questions.question_raw: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV worse than MERS?

parts.text: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV a worse global threat than MERS-CoV?

parts_raw.text: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV worse than MERS?

questions.model_answer: (1) Efficient, sustained human-to-human transmission: SARS-CoV spread worldwide to cause 8096 probable cases in 29 countries, whereas MERS-CoV remains largely sporadic or hospital/zoonotic (camel-acquired), with out-of-hospital family spread uncommon. (2) Greater transmissibility with well-documented super-spreading events and small-particle airborne spread driving rapid global dissemination, in contrast to MERS where an individual case usually infects very few outside health-care settings. (3) Lower case-fatality (SARS overall ~9-12%) versus the much higher lethality of MERS (ICU mortality ~58-78%); a less uniformly lethal virus leaves more mobile, infectious hosts to propagate ongoing chains of transmission.
questions.cohort_conflict: The chapter does not supply R0 values and states SARS patients were most contagious only after lower-respiratory disease developed, so the cohort's 'more asymptomatic spread' claim for SARS is not supported by the text.

cohort_answer.text: Higher R0 (MERS <1, COVID-19 ~3, SARS ~1.5); more asymptomatic spread; less virulent.
